title: Sort app modules by LOC in both directions
preconditions: Start the dashboard with rust-code-analysis-cli available.
Open the Code health view with no file filter.
steps: Select LOC ascending and inspect the first and last LOC values.
Confirm all analyzed app files remain in the register.
Select LOC descending and inspect the first and last LOC values.
Confirm tooling files are excluded from the app source register.
expected: Ascending values never decrease; descending values never increase.
Both sorts cover every analyzed app source file.
The register contains crates/ and web/src/ files, not quality_dashboard/ files.

latest.environment: Codex in-app Browser; local dashboard on 127.0.0.1:4178
latest.notes: Verified live Code health after the latest refactor. LOC ascending and descending are both monotonic across all 78 analyzed app files. Ascending: web/src/vite-env.d.ts (1), crates/desktop/build.rs (3), crates/desktop/src/main.rs (5); descending: crates/desktop/src/state.rs (2,088), crates/core/src/providers.rs (2,022), crates/core/src/tools.rs (1,606). Dashboard reports 2.03 cyclomatic average, 1.45 cognitive average, and 71.8 mean function maintainability index. AST scope is crates/ and web/src/; dashboard tooling is excluded.

title: Open Skills and cancel an unsaved skill
target: Themis web UI in local Vite
preconditions: No Tauri backend is required; do not save the form.
steps: Open the local app and select Skills in the workspace navigation.
Select New skill and inspect the Name, Description, Instructions, Allowed tools, and Scripts controls.
Select Cancel without entering or saving data.
expected: The Skills view and its empty state render.
The new-skill form exposes all expected controls.
Cancel closes the form and returns to Skills without creating data.

latest.environment: Codex in-app Browser; local Vite on 127.0.0.1:5173

Browser-only execution showed expected missing Tauri bridge warnings; native persistence was outside this scenario.

title: Keep suite failures separate from unverified file results
preconditions: Open a recorded Rust run with at least one failed test and inspect the Test register.
Use the current run history; do not alter or rerun product tests during this check.
steps: Inspect the failing file and verify its file-level passed and failed counts.
Inspect a test file with no file-level result in the same failed suite.
Expand its test cases and compare their labels with the recorded run evidence.
expected: A file with an observed failure is labeled Failed with its own counts.
Files without file-level evidence and uncorrelated cases are labeled Unverified, not Failed or Not run.
Suite-level failure totals remain visible without being copied into each file row.

title: Open the packaged app and navigate core views
preconditions: Build and launch the current packaged app.
Use an isolated test project and synthetic data only.
steps: Confirm the workspace opens without a blank screen or blocking error.
Navigate Threads, Skills, Automations, Review queue, and Settings.
Use keyboard focus and the command palette to reach a view, then close the palette.
expected: Each view renders its loading, empty, or populated state without layout failure.
Keyboard navigation and command-palette actions reach the requested view.

title: Create a project, send a thread request, and restore history
target: Packaged app with an isolated local test project
preconditions: Use a disposable fixture directory and a deterministic local test provider.
Do not use production repositories, real credentials, or external provider calls.
steps: Create a project from the fixture and start a thread.
Send a fixed prompt and wait for the complete response.
Navigate away, return to the thread, then restart the app and reopen it.
expected: The project and thread appear in their lists.
The response is complete and remains associated with the correct thread.
Project selection and transcript history restore after restart.

title: Verify approval and review decisions
target: Packaged app with a synthetic approval request
preconditions: Use a deterministic fixture that produces one safe approval request.
Keep any operation that would modify external data out of the fixture.
steps: Open the request and inspect its action, target, and explanation.
Reject one fixture request and confirm no operation runs.
Approve a separate safe fixture request and inspect the resulting transcript/review item.
expected: The dialog presents enough context to decide.
Reject blocks the operation; approve runs only the declared safe action.
The outcome is recorded once and the review queue reflects it.

title: Round-trip a synthetic secret through OS storage
preconditions: Use a new synthetic test key and an isolated provider name.
Never inspect or reuse a real credential.
steps: Save the synthetic value through Settings.
Restart the app and verify only the expected configured status is shown.
Forget the synthetic value and confirm the status clears.
expected: The secret remains in OS-backed storage across restart.
The UI does not reveal the stored value.
Forget removes the synthetic item and the UI reports it absent.

title: Keep no-tool response headers static while streaming
target: Themis app with a text-only game-planning request
preconditions: Open a Themis thread and use a prompt that explicitly prohibits tool calls and file changes.
Observe the conversation while the assistant response is still streaming.
steps: Send a detailed text-only game-plan prompt that prohibits tool calls and file changes.
Confirm the request has no Activities/tool-call trace.
Inspect bold section headers in the live assistant response while it streams.
expected: No tool activity is recorded for the request.
Bold section headers in the live response stay static when no tool is pending.

latest.environment: Codex @Computer; Themis dev app at localhost:1420
latest.notes: Native @Computer first reproduced the issue with a general-knowledge game-plan prompt that prohibited tools: no Activities row appeared, but bold section-label paragraphs shimmered while streaming. The cause was the stale Vite transformed CSS still serving the old .themis-thread-msg--live .themis-response > p shimmer rule after the source rule had been removed. Restarted Vite on port 1420; its served stylesheet now omits that selector and retains the separate action-waiting selector. A fresh no-tool plan produced no Activities row, and completed headings rendered static. During the post-restart run, the capture showed Thinking before answer tokens, then the full answer after generation had completed, so the brief in-progress heading state was not visually captured; marked blocked pending that specific capture.
